prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1263; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The insured reported a left-turn collision at an intersection, and the claimant was identified as the driver of the other vehicle. Initial contact was made with the claimant's attorney, who asked that all communication go through their office.

Entry 2: Photos taken at the scene show the damage to both vehicles, and they confirm several details of the reported impact. No independent witnesses have come forward, so the account rests on the parties and the photographs.

Entry 3: The police report confirms that the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision. The insured's driver is listed on the policy, and the policy was in force at the time of loss.

Entry 4: The damage to the claimant's vehicle is mostly consistent with the described impact. No prior damage to the vehicle is known from our records or the vehicle history check.

Entry 5: The claimant reports a shoulder injury, and the kind and force of the impact appear to match that injury. Medical records show treatment that followed a usual course.

Entry 6: The claimant's account of the collision has stayed the same in each conversation so far, including the initial call, the recorded statement, and the follow-up with counsel.

Entry 7: No earlier injury to the same area of the body is known from prior claims or medical history on file. Nothing in the records suggests the damage existed before coverage began.

Entry 8: Treatment tapered off as the claimant's condition improved, and the most recent provider notes describe steady recovery. The attorney has requested a settlement evaluation based on the treatment records.

Entry 9: Based on the photos, police report, medical records, and consistent statements, the claim appears to be a straightforward left-turn collision. The file is being referred for a settlement evaluation with the claimant's counsel.
